title: Probe-driven replay sanitizer and kernel-fallback policy for stable replay across mixed-shape workloads
author: Anjali Patel
description: Motivation: We saw intermittent replay regressions on mixed-shape production traces where a previously captured CUDA-graph replay would later fail (kernel mismatch or degraded latency) when uncommon shape combinations or partially-warmed KV cache states occurred. Root causes included brittle shape guards that were too permissive, stale kernel mappings when fused kernels change scheduling, and cold-prefix cache interactions that caused different code paths during capture vs replay. Goals: 1) Detect and avoid committing unstable captures with a low-cost validation pass before the capture is used for production traffic; 2) Provide a deterministic, low-overhead fallback that keeps requests making progress when replay is not safe; 3) Reduce warmup variance and tail regressions without adding steady-state overhead. Summary of changes: - Introduce a probe-driven "replay sanitizer" (runtime/cuda/replay_sanitizer.{cpp,h}) that runs a short, representative micro-trace immediately after capture but before the capture is marked eligible for production routing. The probe uses a lightweight instrumentation mode that exercises the graph on a small sample of real or synthetic sequences to validate kernel mappings and output signatures. - Add shape-stability probes: generate compact per-op shape signatures during capture and compare during probe. If the signature distance exceeds a tunable threshold the capture is quarantined. Signatures are intentionally lower-fidelity than full tensor hashes to keep probe latency < 2ms on A100. - Kernel-fallback policy (runtime/scheduler/fallback_policy.cc): per-request deterministic fallback to interpreter/streamed execution when a probe or runtime check fails. Fallback policy includes exponential backoff and a learned retry window to avoid thundering herd on captures that are intermittently unstable. - KV cache primer integration (runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager.cc): when running a probe, we optionally warm prefix KV entries that were present during capture to make the probe reflective of replay conditions. Primer size is capped and gated by a feature flag. - Scheduler coordination: add capture serialization hints to avoid concurrent captures that would create fragmented kernel mapping tables on the same device (runtime/scheduler/capture_coordination.cc). This reduces cross-capture interference observed in production. - Observability: new metrics and traces (replay_probe_success_ratio, probe_latency_ms, probe_kernel_mismatch_count, probe_primer_bytes, probe_quarantine_count) plus debug logs and an integration with Console rollouts to mark captures as "quarantined". - Config + feature gates: feature.gate.replay_sanitizer (boolean), replay.probe_sampling_rate (0-1), replay.signature_threshold (0-1), replay.primer_max_bytes (int). Defaults: sanitizer enabled for canary; sampling_rate=0.05, signature_threshold=0.4, primer_max_bytes=64KB. Implementation notes: - Probes run on the same device as the captured graph to ensure kernel/kernel-selection parity and are scheduled at low priority to avoid interfering with latency SLOs. - The probe uses a stripped-down execution path that replays key ops and compares per-op checksum and shapes; it does not run full model outputs to save time. - We added a small adaptive sampler that increases probe frequency if probe failures spike (heuristic: probe_rate *= 2 up to 0.5) so unstable captures are quickly quarantined. - Kernel-fallback is deterministic: after N consecutive probe-triggered fallbacks, the capture is demoted and traffic routes to the interpreter path until an explicit re-check pass. Testing & validation: - Unit tests for shape-signature generation and match logic (tests/runtime/cuda/test_signature.cpp). - Integration tests that exercise probe + primer behavior under synthetic KV cache permutations. - Canary perf lab runs with production-like mixed-shape traces (bench/perf/replay_sanitizer_bench.py) on A100 and T4; results included below. Benchmarks (summary): - Mixed-shape trace A: probe sampling 5%: median latency: +0.2% (within noise), P95: -12%, warmup variance (measured as stddev of first-100 requests latency): -48%. - Mixed-shape trace B (small-batch heavy): tail latency improved P99 by 34% due to fewer fallback spikes. - Overhead: measured probe CPU/GPU overhead at default sampling is <0.3% of device time in steady-state. Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature.gate.replay_sanitizer on canary region (5%) for 48h. 2) Monitor replay_probe_success_ratio, tail latencies, and error budgets. 3) If stable, ramp to 25% then 100% over 1 week. 4) If probe-induced regressions observed, reduce sampling_rate and re-run before rollback. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Bench scripts + baseline numbers - [x] Feature gate + defaults - [x] Docs snippet for Console and runtime flags Risk & mitigations: - Risk: probe could add latency if misconfigured. Mitigation: low default sampling, runs at low priority, gating. - Risk: false positive quarantines. Mitigation: adaptive sampling and manual override in Console. - Risk: interactions with Dedicated autoscaling. Mitigation: scheduler hints are advisory only. Notes: This PR intentionally focuses on preventing unstable captures from being promoted; it does not change the core capture machinery nor the kernel selection heuristics beyond adding a non-invasive verification pass and a safe fallback. See linked Linear items for continuation work to refine signature fidelity and improve automatic revalidation frequency.

a7d2c1b: implement kernel-fallback policy and integration with scheduler

review_comments: Marco: Concern about steady-state overhead of primers; please add primer_max_bytes cap and ensure primers are disabled when device memory pressure > 80%. Priya: Can we make the signature threshold configurable per-model? Ethan: Suggests adding a counter for quarantined captures per-device to detect noisy devices. Anjali (author): Addressed Marco and added primer_max_bytes gating and a mem-pressure check; added per-model override config and device_quarantine_count metric. Priya: approves after primer cap and per-model config. Ethan: minor nit on log verbosity; fixed. Final approval from Marco and Priya before merge.
release_notes: - Added a probe-driven replay sanitizer that validates CUDA-graph captures before promotion. - New kernel-fallback policy to safely route requests when replay is unsafe. - KV cache primer to make probes reflective of replay conditions. - New metrics: replay_probe_success_ratio, probe_kernel_mismatch_count, probe_quarantine_count. Defaults gated behind feature flag for canary rollout.
performance_impact: reduces warmup variance by 30-60% on mixed-shape production traces; median latency unchanged; tail latency improved for small-batch workloads.
